transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, hi. Um... I guess I'm here because I just feel like I'm always running hot. Like I can't really shut the motor off. And... well, lately it's been getting me into some trouble at the firehouse. So, yeah. That's why I'm here.

Has this feeling of always 'running hot' been a fairly constant part of who you are for as long as you can remember, or is it more like something that comes and goes in distinct stretches of days or weeks?
I don't really know. I haven't exactly kept track of it like that. Um... I'm not sure. I don't spend a lot of time thinking about it, it's just... it's just been an issue lately, I guess.

Thinking back, would you say this feeling of always being 'wound up' or unable to slow down has been part of you since you were a kid, or did it start more recently as a change from how you used to be?

I mean... yeah, I guess since I was a kid. My mom says I was like this back in grade school, too. Just... always out of my seat, blurting answers out. Losing my homework. I used to get a lot of notes sent home back then, even though they said I was bright enough to do the work. So... yeah. I guess it's not a new thing.

Have you noticed a pattern of intense, unstable relationships—like going from idealizing someone to feeling furious or abandoned by them—or a shifting sense of who you are, separate from the restlessness you mentioned?
Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't really get like that with people. And I mean, I know who I am. It's just... like I said, just the restlessness.
Besides the trouble at the firehouse, do you notice this restlessness or trouble focusing causing problems in other areas of your life—like at home, with relationships, or managing day-to-day tasks?

Um... I don't really want to get into my home life. It's... fine. The main thing is just what's happening at work. 

It's... it's starting to cost me trust at the firehouse. I actually got pulled into a performance and safety meeting recently. And... I don't know, my shot at moving into leadership just feels like it's slipping. Mostly because the crew feels like they can't count on me to track the details consistently. So... that's the biggest problem right now.
Have you ever had distinct periods—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or needed much less sleep than usual, separate from your everyday restlessness?
No. I mean... no, not really. I just sleep normal, mostly. I don't get... euphoric or whatever. Just the regular kind of restless.
Aside from feeling restless, do you currently have trouble staying focused on tasks, following through on details, or keeping track of things like paperwork or instructions at work?

Yeah. Um... yeah, I guess so. Like with the paperwork. I'll finish an incident report and think it's... you know, fine. But then the captain will pull me aside and point out I wrote down the wrong unit number, or missed a time stamp. Or I just... skipped some little box that they need for the safety review. So... yeah. That happens.
Do you often find yourself losing track of things you need, like your keys or gear, or getting easily distracted by things going on around you, even outside of work?

Yeah. Um... mostly at the station. It doesn't take much. Like a radio chirp... or someone walking past the bay. Or even just thinking about a call from yesterday. It just knocks me off what I’m doing. And then... I don't know, it just takes me forever to get back on track.
Do you notice this same kind of distractibility or restlessness causing problems for you at home or in your personal life, not just at the firehouse?

Yeah, I guess so. At home, too. It's... hard to just sit around. Like if we're trying to do something quiet, maybe watch a movie or whatever... I can't just sit there. I end up getting up, walking around, maybe going out to the garage to check on my tools. I just start talking or moving. I don't really stay sitting for very long.
